68	- Stop path: B (`RecordingStateViewModel+Stop`) and C (F4 `StopAndTranscribeUseCase`) interact — B's ID threading changes what F4's persistence sees.

unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create -R gitrdunhq/datum \
  --title "[install] installed skill copies missing assets/ — datum.self_check fails on missing hooks + fixtures" \
  --label "datum-bug,bug" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened

Fresh `/datum go` dispatch on the-record-suite (epic-30). Dispatcher step 0.5 runs `uv run scripts/datum.py datum.self_check`, which fails:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "failures": [
    {
      "check": "missing_paths",
      "paths": [
        "assets/hooks/pre-commit-banned-patterns.sh",
        "assets/hooks/pre-commit-file-size.sh",
        "assets/hooks/pre-commit-lane-tools-manifest.sh",
        "assets/hooks/pre-commit-layer-boundary.sh",
        "assets/hooks/pre-commit-tdd-guard.sh",
        "assets/hooks/pre-commit-test-ratchet.sh",
        "assets/hooks/pre-tool-use-install-interceptor.sh"
      ]
    },
    { "check": "contract_fixtures", "output": "FileNotFoundError: .../assets/fixtures/contracts/red-brief.valid.json" }
  ]
}
```

Both installed skill copies (`~/.claude/skills/datum/` and `~/.agents/skills/datum/`) contain only `datum/`, `scripts/`, `SKILL.md` — no `assets/`, `references/`, or `templates/`. The source repo has all three. Sibling of #112 (which covers the missing `references/*.md`): the install step apparently only ships the Python package + SKILL.md.

## Why it matters

self_check is a dispatcher hard stop — every pipeline run on every consumer repo halts at step 0.5 until the user manually repairs the install. The repo-side hooks (`tdd-guard`, `test-ratchet`, `layer-boundary`) also can't be installed into consumer repos if the source `.sh` files aren't shipped.

## Workaround used

```bash
for dest in ~/.claude/skills/datum ~/.agents/skills/datum; do
  ln -sfn /Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/datum/assets "$dest/assets"
  ln -sfn /Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/datum/references "$dest/references"
  ln -sfn /Volumes/Extra/repos/gitrdunhq/datum/templates "$dest/templates"
done
```

self_check then passes (`required_paths: 21`, `contract_fixtures validated: 7`).

## Suggested fix

`install.sh` should copy (or symlink) `assets/`, `references/`, and `templates/` alongside `datum/` and `scripts/`, and self_check should verify them post-install so a broken install fails at install time, not at first pipeline dispatch.
EOF
)"

unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create -R gitrdunhq/datum \
  --title "[contracts] self_test crashes with raw FileNotFoundError when a fixture is missing instead of reporting a structured failure" \
  --label "datum-bug,bug" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened

When `assets/fixtures/contracts/` is absent (see #115), `datum.self_check`'s `contract_fixtures` check doesn't report a clean failure — `contracts.py` dies with an unhandled traceback:

```
File ".../datum/contracts.py", line 131, in main
    sys.exit(self_test())
File ".../datum/contracts.py", line 98, in self_test
    errors = validate_payload(schema_name, fixture_path)
File ".../datum/contracts.py", line 86, in validate_payload
    payload = json.loads(payload_path.read_text())
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../assets/fixtures/contracts/red-brief.valid.json'
```

self_check captures the whole traceback as an opaque `output` string.

## Why it matters

DPS-203 (structured errors): the self_check consumer gets a Python stack dump instead of `{check, missing_fixture, path}`. Burying the actionable fact (which file, why) in a traceback makes the dispatcher-side diagnosis slower, and any tooling parsing self_check JSON can't distinguish "fixture missing" from "fixture invalid".

## Suggested fix

In `validate_payload` (contracts.py:86), check `payload_path.exists()` first and return a structured error entry (`{"error": "fixture_missing", "path": ...}`); `self_test` aggregates these alongside validation errors so self_check emits one coherent failures list.
EOF
)"

unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create -R gitrdunhq/datum \
  --title "[install] uv run from ~/.claude/skills/datum executes the ~/.agents/skills/datum copy — failures misattributed across installs" \
  --label "datum-bug,bug" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What happened

Running self_check from the Claude skill install:

```bash
cd ~/.claude/skills/datum && uv run scripts/datum.py datum.self_check
```

The traceback shows the code that actually executed lives in the *other* install:

```
File "/Users/samfakhreddine/.agents/skills/datum/scripts/datum.py", line 34, in <module>
File "/Users/samfakhreddine/.agents/skills/datum/datum/contracts.py", line 155, in <module>
```

uv resolved the project/venv across installs, so `cd`-ing into one skill copy silently runs another. Both copies happened to be identically broken (#115), but if they ever diverge (partial upgrade, one repaired), you'd debug the wrong files — repairing `~/.claude/skills/datum` does nothing because execution happens in `~/.agents/skills/datum`. I had to repair both copies to make self_check pass.

## Why it matters

Two installs that masquerade as one violate least surprise and make every install-layout bug (like #115) twice as hard to diagnose. Failure messages point at paths the user didn't invoke.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) make one install the canonical one and have the others be symlinks to it, (b) have `scripts/datum.py` assert that `__file__` is under the directory it was invoked from and warn loudly when it isn't, or (c) pin uv project resolution (`--project .` / explicit `pyproject.toml` per install) so each copy runs itself.
EOF
)"

Classify before analysis. This controls how much clarification Refine does.

If you must assume a structural pattern, the ticket is Medium. Ask first.

Batch all questions in one message. Wait for one reply.

For each symbol, API, or module referenced in the ticket:
- GitNexus available: `gitnexus context <symbol>` to confirm it exists

SPEC is sufficient when it answers:
1. What user-visible behavior changes?
2. What are the failure modes and how are they handled?
3. What are the NFRs (latency, size, format)?
4. What is explicitly out of scope?
5. What are the acceptance criteria per requirement?
6. What existing behavior must remain unchanged?

```bash
EPIC_DIR="docs/epics/$BRANCH"
mkdir -p "$EPIC_DIR"
```

Use `assets/templates/SPEC.md` as base. All sections required:

1. Summary (2-3 sentences)

4. Failure modes
5. NFRs
6. Out of scope

So the installed tool rejects the installed template's own format: a SPEC written exactly per template can never pass the installed refine gate.

## Why it matters

Every consumer repo with an out-of-date install hits a guaranteed false-positive gate failure on the first refine of any epic, with a misleading message (there are no open questions). And there is no `datum update` / version check — installs silently drift from the source repo (same family as #115/#117).

```bash
done
```
